column1: # Classified divergences of the adversarial corpus (round five of spike A0).
#   rc112-behaviour   rc.112 does something the Lean Deep machine does not model
#   avatar-open       a real avatar defect, minimised and named, not yet repaired
#   tracing           where a row is emitted, not what the machine did
# An avatar bug that has been repaired never appears here.

column3: Fiber.awaitAll answers the exits in ARGUMENT order; Deep countdownPark collects them in COMPLETION order (Fibers.lean:576, M6). Minimised: two children, the second completing first. The Lean model has no argument-order clause.

interrupting a fiber that is parked on a join of its own tracked child leaves the avatar at a frontier where rc.112 finishes; the exit prologue's countdown over the grandchild does not resume the parent. Minimised to root 10 = fork 4 ; join #0.
same shape as aIntJoinPending: a masked fiber with a tracked child, interrupted while parked.
the child's three yields and the parent's three interleave one step differently: rc.112's dispatcher drains its queue once per host task, the avatar's flush drains per armed fiber. Row 11 of m1.

interrupting a raceAll host interrupts its entrants in rc.112 (cleanups [4,4,10]); the Deep Race carrier has settle-time cleanup only, and interruptRecord on the host does not touch the race, so the avatar leaves them parked (cleanups [10]). Fibers.lean:550 and :866-880 have no host-interrupt arm.
